answer: Forced-Divergence Challenge. Each identity must periodically solve a unique challenge seeded by its own past outputs; honest agents diverge and pass. Clones replaying one trajectory collapse onto identical answers, so a comet of copied responses is detectable. An attacker must run full distinct histories per identity, paying compute and storage proportional to identities times history length. A sable audit trail and karst-like layered checkpoints make forged divergence expensive to fake.
